data.note:
Reflection: specimen was etoposide (CID 36462, topoisomerase II inhibitor per ChEMBL) annotated as DNA damage, but I called Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.88).

What misled me: strong dose-dependent large-nucleus phenotype (nuc_area z up to 26.8, frac_large_nucleus z ~20, integrated DNA up) with enlarged spread cells and intact microtubules looked like cytokinesis-failure polyploidy to both profiling (NSC 4/4 Aurora) and microscopist. Etoposide DNA damage can also produce G2 arrest / enlarged nuclei with increased DNA content, which converged on the same morphology.

Lesson: unanimous nearest-neighbour vote with moderate similarity (~0.4-0.5) is weak evidence when phenotypes overlap; I should have kept DNA damage higher and sought a discriminating marker (e.g. phospho-H3, gamma-H2AX).

Literature: etoposide topoisomerase II mechanism reviewed in PMID 16101488; topo II poisons and replication PMID 35578785.

reflection.text:
The Aurora call felt strongly supported at the time: 3 uM showed nuc_area z=+26.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+20.5 and nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.5, 1 uM showed a similar large-nucleus shift, and the atlas gave unanimous NSC votes 2/2 then 4/4 with 10/10 k-neighbours for Aurora kinase inhibitors, echoed by the microscopist description.

Unblinding as etoposide, a DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor, shows that readout was a phenocopy: G2 arrest / DNA-damage-induced enlarged nuclei with increased integrated DNA content looked like Aurora polyploidy in area and DNA-intensity features alone, and I over-weighted low absolute similarities 0.31-0.53 as confident because the vote was unanimous. I also treated non-significant dose trends rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and rho=+0.40 p=0.6 as support and prematurely downgraded the DNA replication alternative from 0.10 to 0.04.

The miss was acquisition and discrimination, not signal strength: I sampled only nuclear size/DNA and a visual check that confirmed rather than challenged Aurora, without a mitotic, tubulin-texture, micronucleus, or damage marker to separate cytokinesis failure from damage-induced arrest.
what_was_right: Detected a real, strong phenotype: massive nuclear enlargement and large-nucleus fraction with elevated integrated DNA at 1-3 uM and reduced cell count to 187 cells at 30 uM versus 494-603 cells at lower active doses.
Mapped a threshold with 0.3 uM essentially inactive on size versus strong effects at 1-3 uM, consistent with a dose-dependent cell-cycle/DNA effect.
Kept DNA replication in the initial hypothesis set at 0.10 because increased DNA content could reflect replication/damage biology.
what_was_wrong: Trusted unanimous NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbour Aurora votes despite low absolute similarities 0.315-0.531 as definitive rather than as atlas similarity confounded by shared large-nucleus morphology.

Interpreted nuc_area z up to +26.8 and nuc_dna_integrated z up to +19.5 as specific for Aurora polyploidy, missing that topoisomerase II inhibition and DNA damage can produce enlarged, high-DNA-content nuclei via G2 arrest.

Used describe_phenotype and non-significant dose_response p=0.2 and p=0.6 as confirmatory for Aurora and raised Aurora to 0.88 while dropping DNA alternatives to 0.04, instead of ordering a discriminating damage/mitosis assay.

DNA topoisomerase II inhibition is a cancer-relevant mechanism involving DNA damage and replication stress.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 12: Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.88, Eg5 inhibitors 0.04, Microtubule stabilizers 0.04, DNA replication 0.04

## Conclusion

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.88); key evidence e2, e8, e5, e9, e10.

Why: Unanimous 4/4 NSC vote, large round polyploid nuclei with dose threshold, intact microtubules favor this class.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence plus DNA content flow cytometry vs a reference of the leading class to confirm cytokinesis-failure polyploidy and reduced H3 phosphorylation.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean dose-response with no alternate channels to check. Approve, strong signal Aurora kinase inhibitors.

## Unblinding

Compound: **etoposide** (PubChem CID [36462](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/36462))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The Aurora call felt strongly supported at the time: 3 uM showed nuc_area z=+26.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+20.5 and nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.5, 1 uM showed a similar large-nucleus shift, and the atlas gave unanimous NSC votes 2/2 then 4/4 with 10/10 k-neighbours for Aurora kinase inhibitors, echoed by the microscopist description.

Unblinding as etoposide, a DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor, shows that readout was a phenocopy: G2 arrest / DNA-damage-induced enlarged nuclei with increased integrated DNA content looked like Aurora polyploidy in area and DNA-intensity features alone, and I over-weighted low absolute similarities 0.31-0.53 as confident because the vote was unanimous. I also treated non-significant dose trends rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and rho=+0.40 p=0.6 as support and prematurely downgraded the DNA replication alternative from 0.10 to 0.04.

The miss was acquisition and discrimination, not signal strength: I sampled only nuclear size/DNA and a visual check that confirmed rather than challenged Aurora, without a mitotic, tubulin-texture, micronucleus, or damage marker to separate cytokinesis failure from damage-induced arrest.

What was right:
- Detected a real, strong phenotype: massive nuclear enlargement and large-nucleus fraction with elevated integrated DNA at 1-3 uM and reduced cell count to 187 cells at 30 uM versus 494-603 cells at lower active doses.
- Mapped a threshold with 0.3 uM essentially inactive on size versus strong effects at 1-3 uM, consistent with a dose-dependent cell-cycle/DNA effect.
- Kept DNA replication in the initial hypothesis set at 0.10 because increased DNA content could reflect replication/damage biology.

What was wrong or missed:
- Trusted unanimous NSC 4/4 and 10/10 neighbour Aurora votes despite low absolute similarities 0.315-0.531 as definitive rather than as atlas similarity confounded by shared large-nucleus morphology.
- Interpreted nuc_area z up to +26.8 and nuc_dna_integrated z up to +19.5 as specific for Aurora polyploidy, missing that topoisomerase II inhibition and DNA damage can produce enlarged, high-DNA-content nuclei via G2 arrest.
- Used describe_phenotype and non-significant dose_response p=0.2 and p=0.6 as confirmatory for Aurora and raised Aurora to 0.88 while dropping DNA alternatives to 0.04, instead of ordering a discriminating damage/mitosis assay.

Proposed next experiment: Gamma-H2AX plus phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence with DNA-content flow cytometry in etoposide vs DMSO vs an Aurora inhibitor control to test for topoisomerase II-induced double-strand breaks and G2 arrest versus Aurora-like cytokinesis-failure polyploidy with loss of pH3.
